title: Every outside program is optional: one seam per capability, and a setup that lacks one runs without it
description:
bdi reads two programs, bd and herdr, and is about to be public. README
promises "bd, and nothing else" and design.md calls herdr "a provider, not a
dependency". The code keeps neither promise yet. Measured 2026-09-02 at
58e1f79:

- herdr is reached by name from `Collection::collect` (`herdr::agent_list`)
  and wired by name in `tui::wire` (`Herdr::new(RealRunner, ..)`). A machine
  with no herdr gets a foot notice about herdr on every frame of every run.
- bd is reached by name from `app::tracker`, and its argv is known to 155
  test sites across 7 files. A change to one bd flag is a change in all of
  them, and two seats on unrelated beads collide in app/mod.rs's fixtures.
- every project without a credential_command is entered with `direnv exec`,
  the zero-config run included. A machine without direnv reads no tracker.
  README does not name direnv.
- the change probe is `SELECT dolt_hashof_db()`. On bd's default SQLite
  backend it fails on every refresh, silently, at one process each.
- the variable naming the project when there is no config is COMMY_PROJECT.

Graeme asked on 2026-09-02 for the architecture to let capabilities be
optional (no herdr; other ways of reaching beads; other ways of hearing about
changes) and for modularisation that lets seats work concurrently without
colliding. Both have one answer: a seam per outside program, with the adapter
behind it owning that program's vocabulary, its wire shape and its tests.

## What is a seam today, and what is not

    seam                where             adapter        status
    Runner              collect::run      RealRunner     real
    Panes (read,focus)  collect::panes    Herdr          wired by name
    Changes (sources)   tui::wire         Inbound socket private to tui
    View                tui::drive        Screen         real
    collect closure     tui::run          Collection     real
    agent list          herdr::agent_list called directly  missing
    tracker             bd::* called directly              missing
    entering a project  direnv, or credential_command      missing

Runner is at the wrong altitude for optionality. It makes any program
fakeable, but every caller still spells the program's argv, so a fake tracker
is eight canned bd calls and nothing but bd's CLI can be a tracker.

## The children, in the order a public user hits them

1. entering a project needs no direnv (P1, public blocker)
2. the tracker is a seam and app/ stops spelling bd's argv (P1, contention)
3. the agent provider is a seam and a setup with none is silent (P1)
4. a tracker with no Dolt probe stops paying for one (P2, after 2)
5. the project variable is bdi's own (P2)
6. change sources behind one seam outside tui/, with a file watcher as the
   zero-setup producer (P3, after bdi-rer.9 and 2)
7. phrase.rs split by band (P3, contention)
8. forest/mod.rs tests split by concern (P3, contention)

1, 2 and 3 all edit `Collection::collect` and `app::tracker`, so they are
sequenced by dependency edge rather than run at once; 5, 7 and 8 touch none
of those files and run alongside.

## Vocabulary

Neither bd nor herdr names "the thing behind a seam". design.md already
says provider for the agents side and tracker for the beads side; keep
those. Anything a seat has to coin goes in design.md's terminology table.

## Related, not gated on this

- bdi-7ao.65.6 asks whether the layers become workspace crates. These seams
  are the lines such a split would cut along (model and seams; one crate per
  adapter; tui). The seams land first either way.
- bdi-rer.9 is finishing the per-source poll option on top of #30's
  per-project `Armed`; child 6 waits for it.
- bdi-iby is the public epic. Child 1 is a public blocker of the same kind
  as its own, and belongs here because the fix is a seam. bdi-0tp.5, the
  project variable's name, was filed here and moved under bdi-iby: its fix
  is a rename, not a seam.

title: A credential command or direnv that cannot be run is reported on screen as bd's failure
description:
`collect::run::RunFailure::from_exit` classifies the stderr and exit of every subprocess bdi runs, and the screen phrases the result as bd's. A credential command or a direnv that cannot be run (`Exec`) reaches the same mapping through `tracker_env`, so a missing `direnv` or a typo in `credential_command` is drawn as "bd could not be run". The reader is sent to check bd when bd was never reached.

Surfaced by the `bdi-54w.6` seat at https://chat.example.invalid/#narrow/id/41074 while gating cobra's unknown-flag arm on the program being bd; that change covers the new kind only and leaves `Exec` program-blind. Not measured beyond that report.

## Done when

- A failure to run a credential command or an environment tool is reported on screen as that program's, naming which one, and a bd failure as bd's.
- Tested with a runner whose `sh` or `direnv` cannot be executed, asserting the words the screen shows.

title: forest/mod.rs's tests are one module every forest change appends to
description:
src/view/forest/mod.rs is 4,467 lines, of which 540 are production. The rest
is one `mod tests`, and it is where a seat adding a fold test and a seat
adding a motion test both append. 50 commits touched forest.rs before the
split and 8 have touched forest/mod.rs since, measured 2026-09-02 at
58e1f79.

## Shape

A forest/tests/ directory module: `mod tests { mod folding; mod motion; mod
selection; .. }` declared in tests/mod.rs, with the shared fixtures there.
No #[path]: the screen-walks check reads a test module in a file of its own
(dde4449) and cannot follow #[path] (bdi-vtn).

## Done when

- forest/mod.rs is production code and `mod tests;`.
- screen-walks still refuses an unbounded walk in each new file. Prove it by
  adding one and watching the check fail before taking it out.
- cargo-mutants' doubled count is unchanged; lib.rs's cfg pair is its cause,
  not this.

title: Change sources sit behind one seam outside tui/, and a local tracker's files are a producer nobody has to build
description:
Since #30, three things tell bdi a project's work has moved on: a writer on
the inbound socket, the poll each project arms for itself in `tui::armed`
after its own read comes back, and ^R. All three feed one window and one
queue in the loop, and the loop neither knows nor cares which one spoke.
That is the seam; what is left is where it sits and what feeds it.

`Changes` is a private trait in `tui::wire` with one adapter, `Inbound`,
which wraps the socket; `wire` builds it by name. A second external producer
means opening tui/. And the public user's problem stays: README's socket
protocol asks them to build a producer before they get push, and the worked
example is a shell wrapper around bd.

For a tracker backed by a local file (SQLite, or a JSONL export) a producer
already exists in the filesystem. Watching `.beads/` for writes names the
project whose directory moved, exactly as a socket writer does, and costs a
Dolt-backed project nothing: it has no file to watch and keeps its socket or
its poll.

bdi-rer.9 is finishing the per-source poll option in config and on the
command line; it lands first, and this bead waits for it because both edit
`config.rs`, `cli.rs` and README.

## Shape

- `Changes` moves out of `tui::wire` to sit beside the socket in collect/,
  keeping rer.9's names, so a producer is added without opening tui/.
- A file-watch producer per project whose tracker is a local file, enabled
  where the tracker seam's adapter says it is one. Which crate does the
  watching is the seat's to choose against what is maintained now, not from
  memory.
- It feeds the loop the way the socket does, so the window and the read are
  unchanged.

## Done when

- A write to a local tracker's file reads that project without a poll,
  tested with a real file and a fake loop end.
- A Dolt-backed project gets no watcher.
- tui/ names no producer.

title: phrase.rs is one file every screen change edits
description:
src/view/phrase.rs is 554 production lines and holds every word bdi shows,
by design. It is also the file most often in two seats' diffs at once: 24
commits over the crate's history and 10 of the last 60, measured 2026-09-02
at 58e1f79, behind only forest.rs and draw.rs, both since split under
bdi-7ao.33.

The property worth keeping is the one CLAUDE.md names: every word in one
place, under one module name. The property to lose is one file.

## Shape

phrase/ as a directory module with the same `phrase::` surface, split by the
band the words are drawn in (bead rows, project lines, groups and
conflicts, the tail, the foot) so a seat on the tail and a seat on the foot
edit different files. phrase/mod.rs re-exports; the test that checks every
phrase function is reached (the one that binds each to a `fn() -> &str`)
moves with them and still enumerates all of them.

## Done when

- `phrase::` names resolve as they do now; no caller changes.
- Each file opens with a //! naming the band it holds, per bdi-7ao.65.
- The reachability test still enumerates every phrase.
